title: Plain G1: accepted rec7-from-2^48 core, dense X, i.i.d. boot, and a PRICED 10% cap abort: 120.984133965287363

claims.statement: proof.md's algorithm returns x for uniform T=[x]P0 with success >= 0.39 under heuristics H1-H5, H-EA and H-FFT: z=e(T,Q0) against a randomized base g=e(P0,Q0)^b, the charged field map, a=log_g(z) by the GT STNFS core, ba mod r checked by [ba]P0=T. Core: accepted recover-Q 2441acb3 (rec7 record walk per a-run from 2^48; collection <= 2^116.849469000), six owners, N <= 2^58.5430, dense X (28,5) linear algebra <= 2^116.228316314, generator <= 2^107.163, descent meter 2^113.60 with IID_BOOT (fresh exponent and lattice per trial, so trials are i.i.d. by construction). The filtering cap abort is PRICED, not derived: P_CAP = 0.10 is charged flat, so no production filtering law (H3c) is assumed and no Chebyshev extrapolation is used; if N > 0.03330 U the attack aborts and that abort is counted at the full 10% rate. Ledger rows sum to at most 2^117.66220587037693 dense-Fp12 units (C=20,000). All classical work is at most 10 x 2^117.6622058704 + 2^80/2000 < 2^120.984133965287363 G1 units (C=2,000). H-X is not used (dense X). Success >= 0.4987, and >= 0.4587 at +10% expected descent work. Storage below 2^106 bytes; no advice or amortization. Analytic exploratory claim.

experiments.purpose: Hosted audit. {}: code identity, parameters, recorded full-run certificate, integration probes, lazy bound vs a simulation, core ledger and success with P_CAP=0.10 charged, dense-X linear algebra, G1 conversion at 20,000/2,000 with 80-digit decimals, base-randomisation bijection, and the stated ledger-sum inequality checked against a literal constant; {"descent": true} also re-evaluates the descent. evidence16.py (local, ~260 s) reruns every check.
filtsim.py (purge 0.0001, excess 1.05 or 'excess') at the shipped means to weight 100/200/300 (default): +-1 share of row weight (charged 0.86) and U/N, at its scale only (H4u, H3).
